content: 1. Abacavir, dolutegravir, and lamivudine are indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection. The standard dosage is one tablet (600 mg/50 mg/300 mg) taken orally once daily. 2. When coadministered with efavirenz, fosamprenavir/ritonavir, tipranavir/ritonavir, carbamazepine, or rifampin, an additional 50 mg dolutegravir tablet (as a single entity) should be taken 12 hours apart from the abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine dose. 3. This combination therapy is not recommended for patients with a current or past history of resistance to any of its components. 4. Abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine is also indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in children aged 3 months or older, weighing at least 6 kg. However, its safety and efficacy have not been established in children weighing less than 6 kg. 5. Triumeq and Triumeq PD should not be interchanged on a milligram-per-milligram basis. Triumeq PD is for children weighing 6 to <25 kg, while Triumeq is for individuals weighing at least 25 kg. 6. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be coadministered with other antiretrovirals. 7. Emtricitabine and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Coadministration of products containing emtricitabine and lamivudine should be avoided due to therapeutic duplication. 8. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued for at least one month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for elimination of the medications. 9. Antiretroviral medications may also interfere with the manufacturing of betibeglogene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued for at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 10. Sorbitol-containing solutions decrease systemic exposure to lamivudine oral solution, leading to lower rates of virologic suppression, reduced plasma lamivudine exposure, and increased development of viral resistance compared to children receiving lamivudine tablets. 11. Tafenoquine inhibits organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters in vitro, which may increase lamivudine levels. Avoid coadministration with OCT2 or MATE substrates, or monitor for substrate-related toxicities and consider dosage adjustments. 12. Trilaciclib, an OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K inhibitor, may decrease lamivudine levels. Avoid coadministration with substrates where minimal concentration increases may lead to serious toxicities. 13. Abacavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Atazanavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Efavirenz and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Enfuvirtide and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Indinavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Nelfinavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Lamivudine and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ritonavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Tipranavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Lamivudine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Lamivudine and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Lamivudine increases the levels of cabozantinib by inhibiting MRP2 transporters, which may increase cabozantinib toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Lamivudine increases the levels of erdafitinib by decreasing renal clearance. Consider alternatives that are not OCT2 substrates or reduce the dose of OCT2 substrates based on tolerability. 26. Ganciclovir and lamivudine increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of hematologic toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Valganciclovir and lamivudine increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of hematologic toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Ribavirin increases the toxicity of lamivudine through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of lactic acidosis. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 29. Peginterferon alfa-2a and lamivudine increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Peginterferon alfa-2b and lamivudine increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Sulfamethoxazole increases lamivudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 32. Isavuconazonium sulfate, an OCT2 inhibitor, may increase the effects or levels of lamivudine. The clinical significance is unknown. 33. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of lamivudine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 34. Ublituximab decreases the effects of lamivudine through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 35. Givinostat, a weak OAT2 inhibitor, may increase lamivudine levels. Closely monitor if coadministered with orally administered OCT2-sensitive substrates, as small changes in substrate plasma concentration may lead to serious toxicities.
